answer: A cooperative buying saffron from farms on a mesa could give each verified harvest lot one reward budget, shared among every agent handling that lot. Creating a hundred seller accounts would only split the same budget, making effortless sybil profit a fable. An attacker seeking more rewards must obtain more independently inspected crop lots or bribe inspectors, bearing production or corruption costs. Reused lot labels and colluding inspectors remain risks; random physical sampling and a public lot registry help, but cannot guarantee that all sellers have different owners.
